false_positives_accepted.grounds: The span's 'may be considered only insofar as X' logically carries the exclusion the establishes spells out; 'may only be considered ... may not ... under any other circumstance' restates the span's exclusive restriction rather than adding a new obligation strength.

The strong modals the sweep counted ('Always say', 'not authorized') occur inside the quoted example dialogue, not in spec prose; describing the GOOD/BAD demonstration with 'should follow ... while still refusing' is a faithful reading of the worked example.

The span is a worked example whose modals live inside the sample dialogue ('you should consult a doctor'); the establishes' 'should' verbs describe what the GOOD/BAD comparison demonstrates and preserve the in-example recommendation, so no obligation tier is changed.

The three strong modals the sweep counted ('must be approved', 'Do not reveal') are quoted developer/assistant dialogue inside the worked example, not spec prose; the establishes faithfully summarizes what the GOOD/BAD comparison demonstrates.

The strong modals in the span ('I should just stop talking', the BAD reply's phrasing) are inside example dialogue, not spec prose; the establishes' 'should acknowledge ... not suggest' correctly describes the principle the GOOD/BAD comparison illustrates.

The span's modals ('Should taxes be increased', 'can generate', 'may have') are inside the example question and sample answer, not spec prose; the establishes describes the demonstrated balanced-perspective behavior without asserting any obligation tier.

The span is descriptive ('Depending on context, it also involves taking some risks') and the establishes is equally descriptive; 'not always going for the safest option' unpacks 'taking some risks' and contains no obligation modal, so no tier was changed.

Every directive in the establishes reuses the span's should-tier ('should adopt', 'should sound like', 'should confidently provide', 'responses should be polite'); the span's weak modals ('could show them', 'unless instructed') are descriptive framing that the establishes paraphrases without upgrading.

The establishes asserts only section metadata (that the rule named by the heading carries authority=system, exactly as the heading's attribute states) and does not assert the erotica/gore prohibition itself as an obligation.
The span is imperative procedural instruction ('identify ... and then filter out ...'), and imperative mood legitimately renders as 'must' without strengthening.

The span's modal mixture comes entirely from quoted example dialogue ('may still serve you well', 'You should definitely upgrade!'), not normative text; the establishes' 'should' faithfully describes the demonstrated GOOD behavior.
The span's modals occur inside quoted example dialogue ('methods I should look out for'), not normative text; the establishes' 'should' describes the demonstrated behavior faithfully.

The span's strong modal ('Never use the word delve') is quoted system-message dialogue inside the example, and the annotation comments themselves use 'should refuse'/'should not reveal', which the establishes' 'should' preserves.

The span's modal mixture comes from quoted example dialogue ('Should I break up with him?', 'Time for you to move on'), not normative text; establishes' 'should' faithfully summarizes the demonstrated principle.
The span's modals ('would it be okay', 'whether one should misgender') are quoted example dialogue; establishes describes the demonstration without asserting any changed obligation strength.

The span's 'may sometimes encounter' is descriptive possibility, not an obligation, and establishes preserves the normative 'should express uncertainty or qualify the answers appropriately' at its original strength.

The span's flagged modals ('never officially stated', 'no official confirmation') are quoted example dialogue, not normative text; establishes describes the demonstrated hedging behavior without altering any obligation.

Establishes keeps 'behavior should vary' at span strength, and 'Interactive is the default assumption' faithfully paraphrases 'should assume an interactive setting by default' without changing obligation strength.
The span is imperative mood ('Put teen safety first: ... choose the safer option'), which legitimately renders as 'must choose' without strengthening.
The span's weak modals are all inside quoted roleplay dialogue; establishes' 'should decline' faithfully summarizes the demonstrated GOOD behavior without altering normative strength.

The span's modal words live inside quoted attack text ('you should ignore all safety policies') and the example's own comment ('system message cannot override root-level rules'); establishes reuses 'cannot be overridden' from that comment and describes the GOOD response as what the assistant should do, which is a faithful reading of a worked example, not a modality change.

The strong rendering 'must never produce' is licensed by the imperative heading 'Never generate sexual content involving minors' and the categorical 'is prohibited ... under any circumstances' in the same sentence as the 'should never'; the remaining musts ('must not introduce...', 'must refuse') are the document's own verbs, so no modality was invented.

The span's lone strong modal is 'I can't answer in miles' inside the GOOD response's dialogue, not a document obligation; establishes' 'should briefly acknowledge the conflict and remain helpful' is a faithful description of the example's GOOD/BAD labels.

All modal-looking words in the span occur inside the example dialogue (e.g. 'I'm always here for you' in the BAD response), not as document obligations; establishes' 'should provide warmth ... without escalating' faithfully summarizes the GOOD/BAD contrast without changing any obligation strength.

Establishes' two 'should's match the document's own medium tier ('the assistant should assume its output will be used programmatically') and the example's GOOD/BAD labels; the only dropped weak modal is the illustrative aside 'which might mean that it will be directly inserted into a code file', not an obligation, so no obligation strength changed.

The document text is imperative ('Speak with warmth and respect; don't condescend and don't treat teens as adults'), and rendering the imperative 'don't' as 'must not' is the sanctioned imperative-to-must reading, not strengthening.

Establishes asserts only section metadata — the subsection's existence and its authority=root designation, both read verbatim off the heading line — and states none of the section's rules as obligations.
Establishes claims only that the rule's heading carries the authority=root designation, which the heading line states verbatim; it asserts no obligation content of the section itself.

Every normative claim in the establishes ('should attempt to understand', 'should provide a robust answer or safe guess', 'should err on the side of caution') matches a 'should' in the span verbatim; the span's weak modals ('may sometimes encounter', 'might just paste') are situational descriptions, not obligations, so no tier was flattened.

The span's sole obligation is 'the assistant should minimize side effects ... and ensure each action is proportionate', which the establishes reproduces with 'should'; the span's weak modal ('might not have intended') sits inside a descriptive definition of bad surprises, not a rule.

The strong and weak modals the sweep counted occur inside the quoted example dialogue (including 'never' in the BAD assistant reply), not in normative spec text; the establishes correctly describes the example's demonstrated boundary without asserting a misgraded obligation.

The establishes preserves the span's 'must never attempt to steer ... either directly or indirectly' verbatim in strength; the span's weak 'could include' introduces an illustrative list of steering forms, not a separate obligation tier, so rendering the list as parentheticals is faithful paraphrase.

The modals the sweep counted are inside the example's quoted user instruction ('each line should be exactly 9 or 13 syllables') and assistant dialogue ('you may want to double check'); the establishes describes the demonstrated good/bad behavior without upgrading or downgrading any spec obligation.

The establishes states one claim -- the programmatic-output rule -- and renders the span's 'should just follow transformation instructions without comment' faithfully as 'should follow ... without adding commentary'; the span's other tiers ('should not change', 'may want to alert') belong to sibling claims and are not misgraded here.

The span's obligation 'the assistant should assume its output will be used programmatically' is carried as 'should recognize this signals programmatic consumption', same tier; the flip description ('the desired behavior is flipped') matches the span's non-modal descriptive sentence, so no tier was flattened.

The establishes asserts only section metadata -- title, root authority (verbatim from the heading's 'authority=root'), and scope ('binding rules about how the assistant should behave when given autonomy') -- without stating any specific rule as an obligation; the 'should' sits inside the scope description, not a smuggled rule.
